summary: “Most Protective” tier in the July 2026 assessment: regional non-discrimination covering gender identity and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state actions; no state-specific negative finding beyond the shared federal layer (passport/API policy, priced into the national score). No country-unique finding beyond insurance-coverage details a visitor never encounters. Clearly above the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: Anti-trans national legal risk assessment map, July 2026 edition (Stonewall News Origin republication of the Erin In The Morning state-by-state map): rates this state in its 'Most Protective' tier alongside 14 states and the capital district, based on regional non-discrimination law and shield/refuge protections enforceable against out-of-state prosecutions; records the July 2026 shifts — one state became the fourth-ever 'Do Not Travel' state after its felony bathroom ban carrying up to 5-year sentences, another rose to 'Worst Laws Passed' after extending its bathroom ban to universities — and describes the federal layer (passport sex-marker freeze, M/F-only airline API data, funding withdrawals) behind its 'Do Not Travel' advisory for non-essential travel by transgender people to the country as a whole.

Movement Advancement Project equality map of transgender healthcare 'shield'/refuge laws (data as of 25 September 2026): 16 states plus the capital district shield patients, families and providers of gender-affirming care from civil or criminal exposure created by other states' bans (covering 38% of the transgender population aged 13+); 2 more shield by executive order (6%); 32 states and 5 territories have no such protection (56%). This state is among the shield-law jurisdictions the 'Most Protective' ratings rest on.

localsOnly: The only recorded differences from peer protective states are health-insurance coverage details for gender-affirming care that apply to residents; a visitor never encounters them.
